name: Lele (Democratic Republic of Congo)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Kahinyuza Rutinigirwa. 1975. Esquisse grammaticale de la langue lele. (grammar sketch, not online)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page lele1265 and its 26 reference records (Bastin/Coupez/Mann 1999; Boone 1973; Maes 1924; Vansina 1954; Mbaka 1997; CEEBA 1984 volumes; Bukele Ndomay 1985; Douglas/Tew ethnographies etc.)
sources.note: Bibliographic listing only; the only descriptive linguistic items are Rutinigirwa 1975 (grammar sketch), Mbaka 1992 (comparative phonology), Kalunda 1983 and Ngwamashi 1979/1981 (morphology). No source with a stress statement is reachable.

sources.citation: Maes, J. [par L. Achten]. 1934. Vocabulaire des populations de la région du Kasai-Lulua-Sankuru. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 4(2): 209-268.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative wordlist including Bashilele; full PDF (blocked by Persée's altcha) should be checked for any note on accent marking in the transcription — low likelihood of a stress rule.

sources.citation: Torday, Emil & T. A. Joyce. 1922. Notes ethnographiques sur des populations habitant les bassins du Kasai et du Kwango oriental. Bruxelles: Musée du Congo Belge. archive.org item notesethnographi00tord
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bashilele only mentioned ethnographically (refers back to the 1910 monograph); the single 'accent sur la première syllabe' remark concerns the tribal name Bambala, not Lele. No linguistic description of Lele.

sources.citation: Torday, Emil & T. A. Joyce. 1910. Notes ethnographiques sur les peuples communément appelés Bakuba, ainsi que sur les peuplades apparentées, les Bushongo. Bruxelles: Musée du Congo Belge (Annales, sér. IV, t. II, fasc. 1). archive.org item b3136603x
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Chapter 'La langue Bushongo' (p. 252ff) is a grammar sketch of Bushoong (C83), not Lele; comparative vocabularies cover Bushongo, Bangongo, Bangendi, Bakongo, Luchibele with no Bashilele column; the only phonetic remark concerns the consonant 'ph'. Nothing on stress, accent or tone for any variety.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). Lele language (Democratic Republic of the Congo). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lele_language_(Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo)
sources.note: Stub: names, C.84 classification, location, 26,000 speakers (1971); no phonology, tone or stress information; refs only Ethnologue and Maho 2009.

sources.citation: Rutinigirwa, Kahinyuza. 1975. Esquisse grammaticale de la langue lele (leele). Mémoire de licence, Université Nationale du Zaïre (UNAZA), Lubumbashi. iv+94 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The only grammar sketch of the language on record (Glottolog's top-ranked descriptive item); a 94-page Lubumbashi mémoire in the Tervuren/UNAZA tradition normally opens with a phonology section covering tones and accent.

sources.citation: Mbaka Makinda. 1992. Etude phonologique comparative des langues Lele et Woongo. Pistes et Recherches (CEEBA, Bandundu) 7: 131-138.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonological study of Lele; a comparative phonology of Lele and Wongo would state the prosodic system (tone vs accent) explicitly.
